purpose: New-campaign app-only candidate; unbuilt/unmeasured, no live source modification
change: Use ordered likes scan with only SQL lower bound; Goose terminates at first integer post_id greater than the current maximum.
profile_hypothesis: sqlite3VdbeRecordCompareWithSkip consumes 3.62% sampled user CPU (3.24% via range_feed); current upper-bound index check compares encoded keys before the output column is decoded again. Let Goose compare its already-decoded integer, avoiding that encoded upper-bound comparison per row. Some adjacent VM/cell work might also disappear; no measured gain claimed.
invariants: Explicit ORDER BY post_id guarantees that no in-range row follows the first row above maximum.
The lower-bound filter guarantees slot indices cannot be negative; the existing span<256 condition and upper-bound guard preserve the array bound.
The scan is reset immediately on either intentional upper-bound completion or normal SQLITE_DONE; no SQLite error encountered within the requested range is suppressed.
Existing newest-ID discovery, current transaction, per-request counts, output ordering and sparse-range fallback are unchanged.
No rows, counts, responses or tokens are cached, and no schema/index/durability change is involved.
validation_needed: Goose typecheck, official42, parser18 and edge25 on the exact new image.
Additional dense-ID fixtures containing many likes ABOVE the selected maximum, to prove early stopping; include timestamp order different from IDs and in-range IDs omitted from newest20.
SQLite EXPLAIN plan should use the existing covering likes_post_id_idx and no temporary sort.
One bounded matched screen with unchanged controls, then independent confirmation if the screen clears the predeclared threshold.
status: Prepared statically only; no compiler, server, Docker or benchmark executed.
